The awards, presented annually in six categories, recognize excellence in senior achievement, book publishing, article writing, passenger rail articles, photography, and video production. candidates.title: CSX Santa Train sets annual trip for Nov. 21
candidates.excerpt: KINGSPORT, Tenn. — The CSX Santa Train is set to make its 84th trip through Appalachia on Nov. 21, CSX and the North Pole Transportation Authority have announced. The train will follow the 110-mile route through Kentucky, Virginia, and Tennessee that has been a tradition since 1943, delivering toys, gifts, and winter clothing items at stops between Shelbiana, Ky., and Kingsport. “As we look ahead to a new year, we’re reminded that the CSX Santa Train is about so much more than a journey along the tracks,” said Tom Livingston, CSX vice president of government and community affairs. “It’s about bringing people together, creating moments of joy and carrying traditions forward from one generation to the next. The warmth of the communities that welcome the CSX Santa Train and the support from people across the country remind us why this tradition has endured for generations.” Scheduled stops for the Nov. 21 trip include: Kentucky - Shelby, 6 a.m. - Marrowbone, 6:20 a.m. - Elkhorn City, 7:05

candidates.excerpt: New York-listed containership owner Global Ship Lease (GSL) has exercised options for another two newbuildings, taking the George Youroukos-led company’s orderbook to 17 ships. The two midsize, ultra-high-reefer, wide-beam vessels are priced at about $163m in total and are scheduled for delivery in the fourth quarter of 2029. Unlike the first 15 ships in GSL’s newbuilding programme, which have already secured long-term employment, the latest pair remain open. candidates.title: d’Amico brings last leased tanker back in-house
candidates.excerpt: Italian product tanker owner d’Amico International Shipping has exercised a $14m purchase option on the 2014-built MR tanker High Fidelity, paving the way for its entire operating fleet to return to full ownership. Operating arm d’Amico Tankers is expected to take ownership of the 50,000 dwt Hyundai Vinashin-built vessel around mid-January 2027, with the final price subject to a small adjustment depending on the actual transfer date. The ship is one of the last two vessels in d’Amico’s fleet still operating under bareboat arrangements. The company currently controls 28 product tankers on the water — 16 MRs, six handysizes and six LR1s — comprising 26 owned ships and two bareboat-chartered units. The move follows d’Amico’s decision in August to exercise a $15.3m option on sister-era MR High Discovery, which is due to return to full ownership in November. Traffic for the week ending September 26 totaled 235,787 carloads, up 3% compared with the same week in 2025, while intermodal volume of 301,610 containers and trailers was 6.3% higher compared to the same week in 2025. Seven of the 10 specific carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They were led by metallic ores and metals, 9.5%; petroleum and related products, 9.4%; and chemicals, 7.2%. Shipments of farm products excluding grain and food fell by 3.3%, followed by coal, 2.1%, and motor vehicles and parts, 1.8%. Coal inventories are up 1.4 million tons since the end of 2025, while domestic consumption was down 11.4% y/y. candidates.excerpt: RCL books four more container ships at Huangpu-Wenchong The new contract expands RCL’s total boxship newbuilds at Huangpu Wenchong to 16 vessels CSSC Huangpu Wenchong Shipbuilding sealed a new construction contract with Thailand’s Regional Container Lines (RCL) for four units of its inhouse designed "Honghu" series 3,100 teu container ships. The signing took place on the same day that Huangpu Wenchong hosted a naming ceremony for three 4,488 teu container vessels built for RCL, with one of the ships delivered to the carrier on-site. This latest contract award brings RCL’s total container ship newbuilding portfolio at Huangpu Wenchong to 16 vessels, covering three distinct vessel types: eight 4,488 teu boxships, four 1,900 teu feeder vessels and the newly contracted four 3,100 teu "Honghu" units.
